newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 1.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Pleas from West as Hong Kong returned: Western leaders urged China to preserve Hong Kong's freedoms as the former British territory reverted to Chinese rule early today. Page 1.

Opposition leaders blame coalition for dislike of MMP: The behaviour of the coalition government is the reason for the public's distaste for the mixed-member proportional electoral system, according to opposition party leaders. Page 2.
Tougher gun laws likely from inquiry: An inquiry into gun laws, which is expected to recommend tougher restrictions on gun ownership, was presented to Police Minister Jack Elder on Monday. Page 2.
Ministers deny super support: Two National cabinet ministers on Monday denied they supported compulsory superannuation but cautioned against ruling out any scheme till its details were made. Page 2.

Sharemarket soars to six-year high: The sharemarket soared almost 60 points on Monday to a six-year high of 2501 on the NZSE 40 index, reflecting investors' views that the economic slowdown had bottomed and earnings growth was on the cards. Page 14.

Economy falls 0.5 pct in March quarter: The economy fell back 0.5 percent in the first three months of the year -- a worse-than-expected decline showing the extremely weak state of the economy in the March quarter. Page 14.
Fletcher pays A$293m for half of ANM: Fletcher Challenge Paper has confirmed its much-speculated purchase from News Ltd of the half of Australian Newsprint Mills it does not own. Page 14.
THE PRESS

MPs part company on differential issue: Christchurch-based MPs have split along party lines after lobbying by South Island MPs failed to stop the abolition of the power differential from September. Page 4.

$3b arms shopping list denied: The government on Monday denied a Cabinet committee had decided that $3 billion should be spent on buying two more Anzac frigates, modern strike jets, and other equipment. Page 6.

Foreign investment up 14pc to $4b in year to March 1996: Net foreign direct investment in New Zealand rose by more than 14 percent to $4.18 billion in the year to March 1996, from $3.66b a year earlier, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday. Page 33.
CanWest buys More FM network: TV3's owner, CanWest, has bought the MoreFM radio network. Page 33.
Telecom buy-back at $583m: Telecom has spent $583.3 million in its share buy-back programme after completing the second purchase round. Page 33.
Last act in takeover of Defiance: Goodman Fielder said on Monday it had bought the assets of Christchurch-based Defiance Foods Industries. Page 33.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
NZ Post expects go-ahead: The board of New Zealand Post could hear from the government today whether or not it can make a bid for Freightways.

BCL quiet on float rumours: Speculation arising from the budget that the 100 percent TVNZ-owned subsidiary Broadcast Communications (BCL) is to be floated or sold has met a tight-lipped response from management.

Television hardest hit by decline in advertising: Official figures have confirmed what advertising agencies and media organisations have known for months -- last year was the toughest for advertising for nearly a decade.

Govt wants end to Asian wood tariffs: The government plans intensively lobbying Asian countries to abolish tariffs on forest products before a glut of tree exports hit international markets in five yars.

Phillips claims report wrong: Former Pacer Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips rejected out of hand a prosecution suggestion at his fraud trial on Monday that a newspaper report of his views on brokers' short-selling was accurate.
